note: Rewritten from the original description of Froggatt (1898), in English; the original combination was Termes turneri, later placed in Microcerotermes. Alate, queen, soldier and worker are all described, but the original gives almost no measurements in millimetres, lengths being given in lines and inches (1 line ≈ 2.12 mm), and the original units are retained here. Plate 34 figure 8 is the soldier head and 8a the soldier wing.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Entire body deep chestnut brown, the head darkest; antennae brown, paler at the base of each segment; legs and ventral chitinous bands pale brown; wings smoky brown, the veins darker. Length with wings 5 lines, body length 2¼ lines. Head longer than wide, rounded behind, flattened above, the frons arcuate; compound eyes large and round, projecting distinctly from the sides of the head; ocelli round, on the same line as the anterior margin; antennae 13-segmented, short, slender and hairy, set in round pits in front of the compound eyes, segment 1 short and thick, cylindrical, segment 2 very short, segments 3—5 short, round and rather thick, segments 6—12 larger, almost as wide as long, rounded at the base and truncate at the tip, segment 13 rounded at the tip. Clypeus large, convex, lobed, anterior margin truncate, posterior margin rounded; labrum large and projecting, rounded at the tip; mandibles with two sharp teeth at the tip, the lower part forming a broad flat cutting edge, arcuate in the middle. Pronotum not wider than the head, anterior margin truncate and slightly arcuate in the middle, the sides and the posterior margin forming a semicircle; meso- and metathorax large and flat; legs rather long, femora thick, tibiae slender and long, with two large spines at the tip; tarsi long, claws large; wings 4 times as long as wide, rounded at the tip; squama small, the transverse suture transverse, the bases of 4 branch veins visible; costa and subcosta stout, close together and reaching the wing tip; media arising from the subcosta beyond the transverse suture, running parallel through the upper half of the wing and then turning towards the tip, sometimes unbranched, sometimes divided into two branches that fork again near the tip; submedia with 9—11 oblique veins, the basal 5 thickened, the branching unstable. Wings densely covered with fine hairs, forming a fine fringe along the costa. Abdomen long, cylindrical, of even width to the rounded obtuse end, densely covered with fine hairs; cerci very small. Queen paler, the abdominal chitinous plates pale brown, abdomen 1 inch long, 3½ lines in diameter.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale ochre, deepening towards the tip; mandibles rusty at the base and black at the tip, the rest dull white. Body length 2¾ lines. Head very large, longer than wide, rounded behind, the sides rather straight, rounded from the antennal base to the mandibles; flattened above, the frons raised into a convex area divided by a median suture; clypeus narrow, anterior margin slightly lobed; labrum broad at the base, rounded at the sides, covering the base of the mandibles, spade-shaped at the tip; mandibles long and slender, toothless, arising from the middle of the head and crossing each other near the base; antennae 13-segmented, similar to those of the alate. Pronotum small, anterior margin truncate, posterior margin rounded; legs slender; abdomen long oval; cerci small.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head yellowish brown, with dark rusty spots on both sides of the frons. Body length 3 lines. Head slightly longer than wide, convex, with a median suture that branches at the middle of the frons, the branches lying on either side of a horn-shaped spot; the anterior margin of the frons forms a raised crescent-shaped ridge that narrows to a point on each side in front of the antennal bases; clypeus large, convex, divided into two lobes; labrum large, rounded at the anterior margin; mandibles small, with two sharp teeth at the tip and two further large axe-shaped teeth below. Thorax small; abdomen long oval; cerci small and slender.
